construct: Late Treponema pallidum infection can produce tabes dorsalis, with degeneration and demyelination of dorsal roots and posterior columns. Loss of large-fiber proprioceptive input causes sensory ataxia, absent reflexes, impaired vibration/position sense, positive Romberg testing, lightning pains, and Charcot arthropathy.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Late syphilis with lightning pains, sensory ataxia, absent reflexes, proprioceptive loss, positive Romberg testing, and Argyll Robertson pupils is tabes dorsalis affecting dorsal roots and posterior columns.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Spinocerebellar disease can cause ataxia, but it does not explain lightning radicular pains, posterior-column modality loss, absent reflexes, and the syphilitic pupillary finding.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The sensory rather than cerebellar ataxia pattern and neurosyphilis clues isolate dorsal roots and posterior columns.
